cost_projections.limit_source: --limit-s 3600 (the fleet harness log of both pilot jobs (klt-sim-c3ba332c37d3, klt-sim-fd2409da90fb) reads 'running (timeout 3600s)' and both reports say 'job exceeded 3600s'; the manifest's 7200 s is not what the harness enforced)

definitions.assertion: RESETn falls through V_IL starting from HIGH at t0 (Schmitt).  assertion_rail_limited is recorded when VDD itself was <= V_IL at that instant (the output could not stay high regardless of the comparator).  Release = RESETn rises through V_IH.
definitions.baseline: viable when, before t0: exactly one RESETn release and no re-assert, RESETn >= V_IH over the 2 ms before t0, delivered bias branch current > 0 with peak-to-peak <= 5 % of its mean over that window.  Otherwise UNRESOLVED (the dip response cannot be attributed to the dip); detected codes are kept in 'detected_codes_ungraded'.
definitions.delivered bias: explicit measurement: drain current [id] of bias_core XMPIB (PMOS whose drain IS the IBIAS node), saved by the testbench as .save @m.xdut.xbias.xmpib.msky130_fd_pr__pfet_g5v0d10v5[id] and appearing in the klt waveform as i(@m.xdut.xbias.xmpib.msky130_fd_pr__pfet_g5v0d10v5[id]).  Sign: ngspice BSIM4 reports id POSITIVE for normal conduction in both polarities (verified by a local single-corner probe: XMPIB id ~0.78 uA equals the sum of the comparator, output-chain and temp_core diode devices' ids ~0.39+0.39+0 uA at 1.5 ms), so the delivered branch current is +id and must be positive at baseline (else NONPHYSICAL).  The consumer-side diode devices (comparator, output chain, temp_core XMBD [id]) are saved; their sum over the delivered current at the end is recorded (sink_sum_over_delivered_end).  The IBIAS NODE voltage v(xdut.ibias) is recorded separately and never used as a current.  End/baseline ratio band [0.8, 1.25] else FAIL bias_not_recovered.
definitions.detectability: a dip is 'required-to-assert' when VDD spends >= 50 us below V_MUST (piecewise-linear dwell from the full-resolution VDD).  Dips that are not required may assert or not -- both are recorded, neither fails -- but an assertion must still recover.
definitions.expansion policy: No envelope is claimed.  Expansion is a NEW record, never an edit: (a) if a boundary (PASS<->FAIL) appears between adjacent grid levels on any axis, add the midpoint level on that axis only at the affected corners; (a') a middle falling slew (e.g. 10 kV/s) and the 100 kV/s class are added next; (b) falling or recovery slews above 100 kV/s (first: 1 MV/s) need tmax <= 50 ns and a per-request cost estimate (the fleet1 timeout shows cost is binding) before they are added; (c) holds above 1 ms or below 10 us and floors between the three levels are added only with a stated reason; (d) the passive-skew (ll/hh) and mismatch axes are not in this increment.  Any post-hoc addition is labelled as such in its record, as in the #142 diagnosis.
definitions.grid: Floors: 2.0 V is a shallow brown-out above half supply (never 'required-to-assert' under the declared detectability rule), 1.2 V is below half supply, 0.4 V is below V_IL at every starting supply (rail collapse).  Holds span 10 us - 1 ms (two decades).  Falling slews 2 kV/s and 50 kV/s (a ~2 V excursion in ~1 ms and ~40 us) -- two levels a factor 25 apart, kept few because simulation cost scales with 1/tmax and the first 3-level grid timed out on the fleet.  Faster slews (100 kV/s ... 1 MV/s need tmax <= 50 ns) are the first declared expansion (policy b).  Recovery slew is held at 10 kV/s for the full floor x hold x fall cube and varied one-at-a-time (1 kV/s, 100 kV/s) around the center point only -- a declared one-factor-at-a-time treatment of the fourth axis, not a full 4-D cube.
definitions.levels: V_IL = 0.2 vf, V_IH = 0.8 vf, V_MID = 0.5 vf, V_MUST = 0.5 vf (vf = the point's starting supply)
definitions.observation: 10 ms after the recovery edge ends (tstop = t0 + fall + hold + recovery + 10 ms, taken at the largest starting supply): >2.3x the slowest observed release delay (4.3 ms).  A shorter record is truncated -> UNRESOLVED unless a failure is already detected.
definitions.physicality: every saved node within [-0.3 V, vf+0.5 V] for t>0, settled supply current -i(BVDD) > 0, delivered bias positive at baseline.  Violation -> NONPHYSICAL (cannot PASS; behavioural verdict not graded).
definitions.recovery: VDD recovered when >= 0.98 vf after the recovery edge starts; an assertion beginning later is reassert_after_recovery; two or more assertions are reassert_chatter; RESETn must be >= V_IH over the last 1 ms.
definitions.resolution: max sample gap from t0-10 us to VDD-recovery+100 us must be <= min(20 us, hold/5, shortest derived edge/10), AND sampled VDD must match the declared stimulus within 20 mV; otherwise a point with no detected failure is UNRESOLVED, not PASS.
definitions.stimulus: V(VDD) = min(vf, rup*t) - ex*( clip01((t-t0)*sf/ex) - clip01((t-t0-ex/sf-th)*sr/ex) ), ex = max(vf - vlow, 0).  Four independent axes: floor vlow, falling slew sf, hold th, recovery slew sr (+ t0).  The fall lasts ex/sf and the recovery ex/sr: durations are DERIVED from voltage excursion / slew, never a fixed duration, so the swept starting supply does not couple into either slew.  Implemented in the testbench BVDD source (SPICE twin of brownout_checker.vdd_expected, which the checker uses to verify the sampled VDD).
definitions.trace storage: committed traces are change-triggered (dV >= 2 mV on any of VDD/RESETn/POR_RAW/IBIAS node, delivered bias moved >= 2 % of its maximum, or a 1 ms anchor); RESETn assertion/release counts are re-derived from the stored trace and compared with the full-resolution result per point.
definitions.verdicts: ERROR (missing waveform / channel / non-finite data / convergence, model or backend error) > NONPHYSICAL > UNRESOLVED (unviable baseline, truncated, sparse, stimulus mismatch) > FAIL (resolved physical failure, with trace evidence) > PASS.  NOT_COVERED marks points whose request was never submitted, was refused by the fleet, or has no report; they are counted as uncovered, never as PASS.

follow_on:
**This is the tightened-solver PILOT record, not the full re-grade.** Under the cost rule declared in `experiment.json` `tightened_rerun.cost_rule`, two pilot requests (`tightened_rerun.pilot_tags`) were submitted first. Both reached the fleet's whole-job limit. Under that rule the other 19 requests were **not submitted**, so they appear as NOT_COVERED. No tightened point is graded, and the brown-out behavior at the 673 source-NONPHYSICAL points is still **unknown**.

Pilot jobs:

- `control`: job `klt-sim-c3ba332c37d3`, c7i.4xlarge spot, state `timeout`, 3605 s. The default deck took 450 s for the same request (job `klt-sim-c07d9e896014`).
- `cube_v1.2_h0.0001_f50000_r10000`: job `klt-sim-fd2409da90fb`, c7i.4xlarge spot, state `timeout`, 3604 s. The default deck took 1402 s (job `klt-sim-7e1eaffffee5`).

Both pilot jobs ran on runner klt 0.5.0 (client 0.7.0+g04ca88ce427c, `batch.runner_version_check=warn`). The harness log of both jobs reads `running (timeout 3600s)`, so the enforced per-job limit was **3600 s**, not the 7200 s assumed in `tightened_rerun.job_limit_s`. The limit discarded every corner of each job, including corners that had finished (2AMLogic/klayout-tools#2833). All 90 pilot points are therefore ERROR (`batch_job_timeout`) under the existing accounting. They are not UNRESOLVED, because no waveform came back.

Refusal accounting: before the pilots launched, each pilot request was refused five times by the shared fleet's `BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT_INSTANCES=8` cap. klt's `capacity_wait_s` does not wait out that refusal (2AMLogic/klayout-tools#2917), so `run --slot-wait` resubmitted every 300 s. Each refusal is archived and listed per request as an earlier attempt.

Post-hoc diagnosis (not graded, not part of the declared grading):

- The S3 prefix of each timed-out job still holds the per-corner ngspice logs. For `control`, 20 of 45 corners had finished when the limit fired. Of the 8 still running, 7 were 125 C corners. For `cube_v1.2_h0.0001_f50000_r10000`, 10 of 45 had finished. These partial results are not graded: the job report was lost, and grading S3 scraps would bypass the declared harness.
- Two single-corner LOCAL timing probes (`probe --fleet-equivalent`: no `ngspice_init`, so the default SPARSE solver, as on the fleet) ran `control` at ff / 125 C / 2.97 V. The default deck took 19 s (2062 rows). The `reltol2e-4` deck took 389 s (148270 rows). That is about **20x per corner**. The fleet took 90 s for this corner on the default deck, so a whole-request job of the tightened deck projects far past 3600 s. Even one-corner jobs of the slowest default corners (up to 541 s on the fleet) would project past it.
- The same local tightened probe ended with the settled supply current reversed (-1.8 mA at the end). That is the NONPHYSICAL signature, at a point the default deck graded physical PASS. This is a single local debug probe, not a recorded verdict. It does show that the tightened solver can also move a control point *onto* the nonphysical branch.

The projection above applies the pilots' ratio (a lower bound, x>=8.0 on whole-job elapsed time) to every request's default-deck elapsed time. Against the enforced 3600 s limit, all 21 requests project over it. Before any further fleet submission of this variant, a declared decision is needed. Options include: carry `option klu` in the netlist (the repo `sim/spiceinit` sets it, but the fleet runner ignores `ngspice_init`, so every fleet run so far used SPARSE); split requests to one corner per job; run on a fleet with a longer job limit; or declare a less tight tolerance. Any of these is a new declared manifest change, not an edit to this record.

The default-deck record `20261010-222529-41bde9f` is unchanged and remains the evidence for the default deck.
